## Summary

The evidence register is the project's catalogue of sources — official datasets and APIs, tools
and products, other countries' registers, papers and investigations, and the governing law and
licences. Its job is to keep three things separate that are easy to blur: what a source *is*,
what it *claims*, and what has actually been *observed or measured*. Each reviewed source becomes
one compact, append-only row recording what it establishes, how reliable it is, and where it
affects this project. Right now a prioritised discovery queue exists; the reviewed register rows
are still to be written.

The register schema, update rules and discovery queue live in the repository's `literature/`

(schema, §4),

[`companies-house-data-landscape.md`](https://github.com/ThomasHSimm/open-company-uk/blob/main/literature/companies-house-data-landscape.md)

### What a register row records

One row per finished source, with these fields (abbreviated): `register_id`, `source_type`,
`title`, `authors_or_operator`, `year_or_version`, `jurisdiction`, `source_artifact`,
`extraction_file`, `main_question`, `evidence_role`, `operational_proximity`, `access_class`,
`main_data_or_method`, `outcome_or_purpose`, `validation_type`, `current_repo_relevance`,
`future_research_relevance`, `actionability_now`, `supports_production_change`, `main_limit`,
`review_status`, `reviewed_on`, `recheck_by`, `notes`.

**ID prefixes** mark the kind of source: `DATA-` (official dataset/API/register), `TOOL-`
(tool/product), `REG-` (country-register review), `USE-` (paper/report/investigation/repo),
`GOV-` (law/licence/governance), `METH-` (method/entity-resolution/validation).

**Review status** is explicit about how much to trust a row: `solid` (checked, reliable for its
role), `conditional` (usable with a stated caveat), `needs-review` (do not rely on without
revisiting), `screening-only` (not accessible enough for full extraction), `rejected`,
`inaccessible`, `superseded` (access/schema/pricing/law changed — the old observation is kept and
the replacement linked).

### The guardrails the register enforces

The point of the register is disciplined honesty, so its update rules are strict: append-only by
default; never silently change an earlier judgement (add a dated note or a superseding row); do
**not** upgrade a `claimed` finding to `observed` or `measured`; an official source *defines* a
field or access rule but does not thereby *validate* an analytical indicator; a vendor source
supports what the vendor claims to offer, not independent effectiveness; and keep
data-existence, capability, observed use and measured validity separate.

> **Why this matters here.** The same discipline runs through the whole site: figures are labelled
> **[Checked] / [Estimated] / [Not verified]**, and the [indicators](../indicators/methodology.qmd)
> ship only what traces to a named field. The register is where that discipline is applied to the
> evidence base itself.

### The discovery queue (current)

These sources are **identified and prioritised, not yet reviewed** — they do not have register
IDs. The top of the recommended first-extraction order:

| # | Source | Role | Why first |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | Companies House Public Data API reference + OpenAPI spec | Official definition | Canonical endpoint/resource inventory; anchors the data dictionary |
| 2 | Companies House `api-enumerations` | Official definition | Canonical status/PSC-statement constants; schema-drift tests |
| 3 | Charges list resource | Official definition | Directly relevant to the `CHARGES_OUTSTANDING` rule |
| 4 | CH data products / download portal / daily PSC snapshot | Official definition | Establishes the bulk routes for population context |
| 9–11 | BEIS PSC-register review; 2nd PSC-regulations review; Jofre & Knobel (2025) | Measured / evaluation | Closest methodological matches to this project |
| 12 | Clatworthy & Peel (2016), UK private-company filing timeliness | Academic (measured) | Evidence for the late-filing work; separates behaviour from prediction |

The main conclusion from discovery, recorded verbatim in the queue: the strongest starting
evidence is **not** a conventional academic literature but a combination of official schemas and
guidance, official evaluations and statistics, a small empirical PSC/filing/disqualification
literature, and investigative/vendor material that shows possible uses but usually cannot validate
an indicator. The current rule set is therefore defended as a **transparent representation of
registrar-recorded states**, not as a validated fraud, trustworthiness, credit or
insolvency-prediction model.

### What's next

As each queued source is read and extracted, it becomes one reviewed row here, following the rules
above. Until then this page is the structure and the queue; the [prior-work page](prior-work.qmd)
summarises the investigations and tools already drawn on.
